content:
Sophia: Quick thread — seeing intermittent drops in quality when the runtime switches to INT8 for mid-length requests (~256-1024 tokens). The switches look correlated with short bursts of load, but the quality dips are bigger than expected. Thoughts on smoothing the precision transitions and what telemetry we should add?

Ravi: Hmm, is the switch happening per-request or per-connection?

Sophia: per-request, based on current profile scoring. We let the runtime pick the cheapest acceptable profile and it flips when profile score crosses threshold.

Josh: Two quick tactics that helped us before: (1) temporal smoothing (moving avg of quality metric) so we don't flip on a single noisy sample, (2) hysteresis with a minimum dwell time.

Tara: +1. Also shadow-run a small fraction of INT8 requests through FP8 (or baseline) to have continuous ground truth for drift detection. Sampling rate doesn't need to be huge — 0.5-2% usually enough.

Kevin: For telemetry naming, let's emit events: quant.switch_attempt, quant.switch_commit, quant.rollback, quant.quality_sample. Payloads: {model, endpoint, requested_profile, candidate_profile, quality_metric, token_len_bucket, latency_ms, trace_id}.

Sophia: example payload would help, Kevin — can you paste a minimal JSON?

Kevin: Sure:
```
{
  "event": "quant.switch_commit",
  "model": "redwood-v1",
  "endpoint": "/generate",
  "from": "fp8",
  "to": "int8",
  "quality_metric": 0.874, // moving avg at commit time
  "window_s": 60,
  "token_len_bucket": "256-512",
  "latency_ms": 78
}
```

Ravi: For smoothing algorithm: I'd propose an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of the last N quality samples per endpoint+profile+len_bucket, plus a short absolute sample count guard (e.g., require >= 10 samples in window). That avoids being overconfident with sparse data.

Josh: And for dwell/hysteresis: require a minimum commit duration (min_dwell_ms) and a rollback_threshold larger than the commit threshold (asymmetric). Eg: commit if delta > 1.5% for 30s, rollback if delta < -2.5% sustained 30s. This gives slack to avoid flip-flop.

Tara: Tradeoffs: longer dwell reduces oscillation but increases cost if we stick to FP8 unnecessarily. We should expose eta: cost_penalty_ms or token_cost_estimate when making decisions — so decision can be framed as utility = quality_gain - lambda * cost_penalty.

Sophia: Nice. Let's write defaults we can start with and tune:
```yaml
precision_smoothing:
  window_seconds: 60
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
  min_sample_count: 12
  min_dwell_ms: 30000
  commit_delta_pct: 1.5
  rollback_delta_pct: 2.5
  rollback_sample_rate: 0.01 # shadow-run fraction for rollback verification
```

Kevin: One operational detail: emit a metric for "quant.dwell_violations" so oncall can see when we kept a profile past its expected dwell (useful for debugging overrides).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staged rollout of smoothing feature to canary cluster started at 2026-03-22T15:20Z :rocket:

Josh: We also need SLO guardrails: if quality drops by >5% for 5m on any customer, force immediate rollback and page. Keep that out-of-band from normal smoothing logic.

Tara: Will set up shadow evaluation job for two endpoints with 1% sampling and run overnight to collect baseline deltas.

Sophia: Action items: (1) I will open an RFC PR with the tuning defaults above + examples of telemetry payloads, (2) Tara will create the sampling jobs, (3) Kevin will add event schema to tracing docs, (4) Josh will add SLO-guard that bypasses smoothing for severe degrade.

Kevin: SGTM. Can we also log the raw request hashes (or shards) for failed rollbacks for offline bisecting? Keep hashes salted and ephemeral.

Sophia: yes — store only short salted fingerprints and trace_id. No PII.

Ravi: One more thought: for multi-turn chat we might prefer a session-level stickiness (per-conversation precision tag) to avoid toggles mid-chat. Might be separate feature but worth calling out.

Sophia: Good call. I'll add a note to the RFC about session stickiness and its cost implications.

Josh: :thumbsup:

Tara: I'll drop the first run results here tomorrow.

Sophia: Thanks team — this should cut oscillation without too much added cost if we tune carefully.
